answers.why: Moses calls all Israel and addresses them as witnesses of the events in Egypt.
Israel comprises the men assembled with their tribal leaders, elders, and officers.
Moses speaks to all Israel and then addresses them in the plural.
All Israel witnesses Moses commissioning Joshua to lead this people into their land.
The elders of Israel receive the law from Moses alongside the priests.
All Israel assembles before the LORD at the appointed festival.
The law is read in their hearing, with men, women, and children gathered.
Moses finishes addressing the people and tells them to instruct their children.
Moses blesses Reuben's survival and the number of its men among the gathered tribes.
Moses blesses Levi's priestly role, and the following verse describes their covenant obedience.
The Levites will teach Israel the law as their national priestly duty.
Moses blesses Benjamin with secure dwelling in his blessing of the tribes.
Ephraim's ten thousands are the collective force that pushes other peoples.
Manasseh's thousands form part of the collective force described in Joseph's blessing.
Moses introduces Zebulun's tribal blessing, followed by collective activities in the next verse.
Zebulun is addressed collectively, with the next verse describing what they will do.
Moses introduces Gad's tribal blessing concerning expansion and military strength.
Gad is enlarged and depicted as a fighting lion in the tribal blessing.
Gad acts with the leaders of the people and carries out the LORD's judgments with Israel.
Moses introduces Naphtali's tribal blessing and commands possession of territory.
Naphtali is addressed as the tribe that will possess the west and south.
Moses introduces Asher's blessing among the other tribal blessings.
Asher receives a tribal blessing of favor among its brothers and abundance of oil.
Israel dwells securely in fertile land after its enemies are driven out.
Israel is explicitly called a people saved by the LORD.
